text:
liam_sales: Quick thread for AtlasBank POC ask — they want: 1) EU-only processing & cache for EU tenants (including during automated failover), 2) list of subprocessors & certs for Sao Paulo region, 3) whether support engineers can access EU data from non-EU IPs, and 4) a rough hosted vs dedicated delta for 200 and 750 RPS.
nuria_se: TL;DR: we support tenant pinning and region-constrained failover. Key knobs: tenant_pin, failover_mode, on_no_region_capacity. If tenant_pin=true + failover_mode=region_fallback_only then compute + KV cache remain within allowed region set. If no eligible region remains, options: reject requests (503), degrade (no KV cache reads), or allow cross-region with escalation.
mike_infra: Subprocessors in sa-east1 (Sao Paulo): GCP (sa-east1) — customer-facing certs: https://gcp-example-cert.link, LogStream (logs stored in sa-east1), TelemetryCo (metrics), and SIEM partner (SOC2 available). We can export a CSV of vendor + cert links. We don't currently host a dedicated BR-only zone, hosted runs in sa-east1 for LATAM.
carmen_priv: On legal: we can do DPA + SCCs. For LGPD we can add an addendum that prohibits cross-border processing for EU-flagged tenants unless explicit legal exception. We can also state that support access is limited to auditors on EU IP allowlist and is logged; emergency access requires documented approval sequence.
pedro_customer: Can you confirm cache behaviour? They are worried that KV shards might replicate to US during DR. Also: what is RTO if EU region is saturated?
nuria_se: Cache semantics (short): primary KV cache is region-local when tenant_pin=true. Background metadata backups to control plane are configurable for region-only retention for the POC; replication to other regions only occurs if on_no_region_capacity is set to allow_cross_region or during manual DR ops. RTO: if failover_mode=region_fallback_only and no EU capacity, we can: a) return 503 immediately (fast, safe), b) fall back to a degraded write-only mode (reads hit cache miss) or c) failover to dedicated EU capacity if pre-provisioned. Pick (a)/(b)/(c) in routing policy.
nuria_se: routing example for the POC:
```
routing_policy:
  allowed_regions: ["eu-west-1","eu-central-1"]
  tenant_pin: true
  failover_mode: "region_fallback_only"
  on_no_region_capacity: "reject"   # reject == return 503
```
nuria_se: curl to create tenant for POC:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"tenant_id":"atlas-eu","region_pin":"eu-west-1","routing_policy":{"failover_mode":"region_fallback_only","on_no_region_capacity":"reject"}}'
```
mike_infra: Pricing (very rough): Hosted with tenant_pin — pricing same per-token, but we can reserve transient capacity for POC windows. Dedicated (reserved capacity) sketches: ~ $28k/mo for 200 RPS baseline (depends on model family & q8/q4), ~ $110k/mo for 750 RPS with enterprise support and reserved GPUs. We'll follow up with formal quote.
liam_sales: Action items: 1) mike_infra: export subprocessor CSV + cert links for sa-east1 and SOC2 docs (today) 2) carmen_priv: draft LGPD addendum language and support-access clause (today) 3) nuria_se: confirm routing snippet is valid for hosted POC infra and test reject behavior on staging (ETA 3 hours) 4) mike_infra: sketch dedicated quote (ETA EOD).
bot-deploy: POC org created: redwood-poc-atlasbank-1924009999. Endpoint: https://eu.api.redwood.ai/poc/atlas-eu. Credentials provisioned to vault.
pedro_customer: Thanks team — they'll also request supplier evidence for LogStream (logs) and TelemetryCo (metrics). Please include contact + cert links in CSV.
liam_sales: Will send a short email to AtlasBank with the CSV + DPA draft and routing sample once we have it. Target to send by EOD.
(End of thread)
